newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares dip at noon on poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares dip at noon on poor sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares dipped at midday on Wednesday on poor market sentiment despite institutional support for market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development, brokers said.
The index shed $0.114 points or 0.24 percent to 47.021 points, on volume of 2.0 million shares worth $840,000. Of 41 B shares, 25 traded, with nine down, 11 flat and five up.
Brokers said institutional support for Shanghai Lujiazui failed to stimulate investor interest, with liquidation, mainly from institutions, emerging again.
Shanghai Lujiazui traded the most, edging up $0.002 or 0.22 percent to $0.882, on volume of 465,500 shares.
"Market sentiment has been very poor, with few buying orders in the market," one broker said. "If there is no policy support from the authorities, the market will fall further."
"If Lujiazui cannot maintain its current price, the market is likely to set a record low in the afternoon," a second broker said.
Huaxin Cement was the biggest loser on expectations of its unpromising results, falling $0.010 or 5.00 percent to $0.190, on volume of 30,000 shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development followed, falling $0.010 or 2.63 percent to $0.370, on volume of 21,000 shares.
Shanghai A shares fell on jitters over possible negative news, brokers said.

The A index fell 18.843 points or 1.93 percent to 957.384 points, on volume of 156.4 million shares worth 1.4 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index dipped 49.806 points or 2.03 percent to 2402.053 points.
Dalian Beida Vehicle Trades was the biggest loser on profit-taking after rises in the past few days, falling 1.00 yuan or 6.36 percent to 14.70 yuan on volume of 489,100 shares.
